subject: Urgent: Reserved throughput alarm — QuantumPay latency & error spike
messages:
From: Ethan Long <ethan.long@quantumpay.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@quantumpay.com
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Significant latency + 500s errors — reserved throughput appearing capped

Rishi —

We started seeing a sharp rise in latency and 500s around 17:45 PT. P95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s and error rate for the /generate endpoint is about 4.8% over the last 30m. Our app is reporting queuing at the client side and some requests never return.

We have an active reserved capacity contract and our dashboard shows our reserved throughput never exceeds ~70% of the committed value — we’re effectively throttled even though we’re within our reservation. This is impacting checkout flows; we’re seeing failed auth attempts and payment retries.

Sample request IDs attached (qpay_error_sample_20280419.log). Can you confirm if this is a Redwood-side saturation or something on our end? We need immediate help — this is impacting live payments.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Long
Head of Platform Engineering, QuantumPay
ethan.long@quantumpay.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Long <ethan.long@quantumpay.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 18:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Significant latency + 500s errors — reserved throughput appearing capped

Ethan — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I’m escalating immediately.

What I’m doing now (short actions):
- Looping in Priyom (serving/runtime) and Naomi (SRE) to triage GPU pool behavior and routing.
- Requesting your top 10 failing request IDs (if different from attached) and a timeframe window — already pulled the sample you attached.
- Temporarily enabling emergency routing (move a fraction of traffic to a lower-memory model variant) and checking reserved reservation mapping.

Please expect a follow-up in 20–30 minutes with initial findings. I’ve attached a quick diagnostic checklist and what we’ll need: runbook_temporary_fallback.md (internal).

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Customer Engineering, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Ethan Long <ethan.long@quantumpay.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 18:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Significant latency + 500s errors — reserved throughput appearing capped

Ethan / Rishi —

Quick notes from infra side after correlating metrics:
- GPU pool for the us-west-2 reserved partition for QPAY shows sustained GPU saturation on 3 nodes; aggregate utilization is ~92% with queue depth rising.
- We see long-lived KV cache residency for your conversational workload (session pinning) causing fewer slots for short requests. A burst of long sessions earlier (around 17:30) amplified queueing and triggered backpressure in the scheduler.

Immediate mitigation I can enact now (30–45m):
1) Spin up 2 temporary burst instances (reserved-burst) and route ~30% of QPAY traffic there (will honor reservation but on different pool) — short-lived and audited.
2) Canary lower-memory model variant (v1-lite-quant) for non-critical traffic (auth/quote endpoints) with 20–30% traffic.
3) Apply token limit override for chat sessions: reduce max_context_tokens from 4096 to 2048 for 10m window to clear KV pressure.

I’m preparing the exact commands and will push them once Rishi approves. Attaching runbook_temporary_fallback.md (commands + rollback).

—Priyom
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
priyom@redwood.ai
From: Ethan Long <ethan.long@quantumpay.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 19:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Significant latency + 500s errors — reserved throughput appearing capped

Thanks — that plan sounds good. We’re attaching another 30m of edge logs and an SRE trace (ops@quantumpay.com).

Couple quick asks:
- Timeline: how long to see measurable improvements after the routing change? We need to revert quickly if anything causes regressions.
- SLA credits: our finance/ops team is already flagging the outage window — who do we talk to for a formal service credit request if this impacts revenue?

We can enable any sampling you need on our side.

Ethan
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Long <ethan.long@quantumpay.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 20:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Significant latency + 500s errors — reserved throughput appearing capped

Update for the thread — mitigation actions executed at 19:50 PT:
- Deployed 2 reserved-burst instances and routed ~30% of QPAY traffic to them.
- Canaryed v1-lite-quant for non-critical flows (auth/quote) at 25% traffic.
- Enforced temporary context cap for active chat sessions (4096 -> 2048).

Early signals: p95 latency for the /generate endpoint has fallen from ~1.2s to ~300–380ms in the last 10 minutes; error rate down from ~4.8% to ~0.6%. CPU/GPU queue depth reduced noticeably.

Next steps:
1) We’ll keep the burst instances for 4 hours while we run an RCA and validate stability.
2) Priyom and Naomi are collecting scheduler traces (link in related_links) and I’ll prepare an incident summary for exec review.
3) Lauren — please coordinate with finance on an SLA credit request; I’ll provide timestamps and impact windows.

Attaching mitigation_summary_20280419.pdf for your ops team. Please confirm if there are any regressions after the route change.

Rishi
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary: QuantumPay reserved throughput incident (impact, remediation, next steps)

Quick executive readout for leadership — setting up a follow-up with finance and account execs.

Impact: QuantumPay (deal QPAY-4231) experienced an elevated latency and error spike on 2028-04-19 starting ~17:30 PT with p95 latency rising to ~1.2s and error rate ~4.8% for ~30–40 minutes. This affected critical checkout/auth flows and resulted in customer reports of failed payments.

What we did: emergency routing to burst instances, canaryed a lower-memory model, applied temporary context caps. Early telemetry shows p95 improved to ~300–380ms and error rate reduced to ~0.6% within 15 minutes post-mitigation. Mitigation window started at 19:50 PT.

Open items / next actions:
1) Full RCA (ownership: Priyom) with scheduler traces and KV cache analysis — due EOD 2028-04-20.
2) Permanent capacity decision (ownership: Naomi + Capacity org) — do we expand QPAY reservation or create a dedicated headroom pool? Concern: cost vs SLA stability.
3) SLA credit review & customer comms (ownership: Lauren + Rishi) — need financial approval and agreed statement to send to QuantumPay.
4) Improve detection: add a reserved-throughput saturation alert that triggers before queue depth crosses threshold (ownership: SRE/Monitoring).

I’ll schedule a 30-minute sync with the appropriate stakeholders later today. Rishi — please include the incident timeline and logs for the credit request.

—Lauren
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
